records.reason: Nitrobenzophenone at 2/1 and 100 uL, predicted 5.54/12.81 mL, starts a matched-loading pair with the selected 5/1 condition. Existing 10/1 and 50/1 measurements at this amount have an unusual completion ordering. Stronger-eluent anchors can constrain that response without treating it as a universal solvent rule.

Complete the nitrobenzophenone 2/1-to-5/1 pair at 100 uL, predicted 8.11/19.49 mL. Together with existing same-loading measurements, this tests whether the conflicting weak-eluent behavior is preceded by an ordinary increase or a broader nonmonotonic pattern.

Para-aminobenzonitrile at 2/1 and 50 uL is predicted at 14.47/41.29 mL. Its measured 1/1 condition uses the same amount, while the recent 5/1 observation at 100 uL established much later completion. This locates the intervening transition while retaining the loading difference.

Meta-aminobenzonitrile at 2/1 and 100 uL, predicted 12.69/39.59 mL, matches its measured 5/1 loading. This tests transition shape after a substantial historical completion underestimate and complements the para-isomer experiment, whose amount differs.

4-Methylquinoline at 5/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 30.42/65.17 mL. Its measured coverage is restricted to stronger eluent. This tests substitution transfer from quinoline within fused basic heteroaromatics, where other nitrogen families have required different correction directions.

2,6-Lutidine at 5/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 21.00/54.73 mL. Its measured 10/1 condition at 150 uL establishes substantial completion volume. This tests an intermediate response for a sterically shielded pyridine nitrogen, retaining the amount difference.

Ethyl aminocrotonate at 10/1 and 50 uL with DCM loading is predicted at 28.99/87.86 mL. The measured 20/1 condition has identical loading. This tests how much of its large response develops before 20/1 and whether an enamine ester shares response shape with aromatic amino-carbonyl compounds.

Acetophenone oxime at 20/1 and 50 uL is predicted at 23.65/55.74 mL, beyond its same-loading 5/1 coverage. This tests an unanchored transition in an N–O donor/acceptor environment that need not follow either amine or alcohol response scales.

The cyclopropyl beta-ketoester at 10/1 and 100 uL, predicted 30.81/63.46 mL, matches its recent 20/1 loading. That measurement exposed a large historical underestimate. The intermediate label determines whether the newly established response develops mostly before or after 10/1.

Methyl acetoacetate at 20/1 and 50 uL, predicted 14.69/34.19 mL, extends its same-loading 5/1 observation. This provides a simple beta-ketoester response against which to interpret the larger cyclopropyl and methoxyethyl responses.

The alpha-benzyl beta-ketoester at 20/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 25.05/49.24 mL. Existing coverage is confined to pure EA at another amount. This tests transfer to substitution between the carbonyl groups without asserting an unspecified tautomeric mechanism.

The methacrylate/acetoacetate diester at 10/1 and 150 uL, predicted 31.18/69.97 mL, matches its measured 1/1 and 5/1 loading conditions. This tests whether the large methoxyethyl-acetoacetate response transfers to a different multi-oxygen arrangement.

Tert-butyl acetoacetate at 10/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 10.11/22.03 mL. Its measurements predominantly anchor stronger eluent. This tests whether changing the ester-side steric environment gives a modest response despite the larger responses of other beta-ketoesters; existing anchors use different amounts.

Benzoylacetone at 50/1 and 100 uL, predicted 21.63/49.47 mL, extends its matched 20/1 measurement. The proposed increase tests weak-eluent transfer from beta-ketoesters to a beta-diketone after the earlier 20/1 prediction overestimated retention.

3-Phenylpropanol at 5/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 31.80/61.21 mL. Its measured 10/1 condition at 150 uL establishes a large response. This fills an intermediate region for a primary alcohol without an additional ring substituent, retaining the loading difference.

4-Phenylbutan-2-ol at 5/1 and 50 uL, predicted 22.21/37.44 mL, forms a fixed-loading pair with its selected 2/1 condition. The pair tests a remote secondary hydroxyl environment against measured primary-alcohol responses and compact constrained-alcohol intervals.

Complete the 4-phenylbutan-2-ol pair at 2/1 and 50 uL, predicted 15.73/30.59 mL. Two labels at fixed loading identify a local slope and test whether the steep response measured for methoxyphenethyl alcohol transfers to this secondary alcohol.

1-Phenylethanol at 5/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 9.55/19.81 mL, below both endpoints of its same-loading 2/1 measurement. Testing this proposed dip can expose incorrect sharing of solvent-response behavior between benzylic and remote alcohol environments.

Benzyl benzoate at 50/1 and 50 uL, predicted 11.98/24.98 mL, bridges matched-loading measurements at 30/1 and 100/1. The latter exposed a large historical onset underestimate. This distinguishes gradual onset growth from a transition concentrated beyond 50/1.

Cinnamic acid at 2/1 with 1500 uL DCM loading solvent is predicted at 12.16/43.57 mL. Together with its selected 5/1 condition and the measured 2000 uL series, this tests a recorded loading-solvent feature at two ratios. The recorded densities differ slightly.

Complete the cinnamic-acid 1500 uL loading-solvent series at 5/1, predicted 16.23/58.03 mL. The paired ratios distinguish a solvent-response comparison from a loading-solvent-volume comparison and test whether the broad measured intervals transfer between the supplied loading conditions.

The formally charged P/O structure at 5/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 20.30/40.84 mL. Matched-loading measurements at 2/1 and 10/1 bracket a large rise. This identifies curvature in a rare atom environment without assuming unspecified solution speciation.

Para-methoxyacetophenone at 10/1 and 100 uL, predicted 23.91/46.30 mL, extends its matched 2/1 observation. It tests the proposed strong response in a common aryl-ketone family against the distinct measured methylthio-ketone behavior.

The methoxy-hydroxybenzaldehyde at 20/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 19.17/38.05 mL. Its measured 50/1 condition uses identical loading. This tests the intermediate response of an ortho-hydroxyl carbonyl environment and its transfer from simpler carbonyls and alcohols.

The two-carbonyl diaryl compound at 5/1 and 100 uL, predicted 5.32/19.43 mL, precedes matched measurements at 10/1 and 20/1 that exposed different historical error directions. This constrains response shape before its larger weak-eluent rise.

Cyanobenzophenone at 20/1 and 50 uL is predicted at 30.57/64.94 mL. Its measured 5/1 and 50/1 conditions establish a large overall response at larger amounts. This tests its proposed transition and structural transfer from nitrobenzophenone while retaining the loading differences.

Mesityl methyl ketone at 20/1 and 50 uL is predicted at 7.53/22.08 mL. Measured coverage is confined to stronger eluent at other amounts. This tests whether proximal methyl substitution preserves a modest onset while completion expands, complementing the measured branched and cyclic ketones.

Unmeasured biphenyl-substituted butyrophenone at 5/1 is predicted at 6.09/13.68 mL. It starts a fixed-loading pair with its selected 20/1 condition. Two labels test whether extending the aromatic system preserves the modest response of alkyl aryl ketones.

Complete the biphenyl-substituted butyrophenone pair at 20/1 with identical loading, predicted 5.65/18.10 mL. This tests the proposed nearly constant onset with increasing completion in a new scaffold, using common alkyl aryl ketones and biphenyl aldehyde as structural references.

Unmeasured para-chloroanisole at 50/1 and 150 uL is predicted at 6.00/13.65 mL. Related halogenated-anisole observations provide structural references. This tests low-retention transfer and guards against extending larger multi-ether responses to every aromatic ether.

Unmeasured bromodimethoxybenzene at 20/1 and 50 uL is predicted at 8.80/20.41 mL, with observed similarity 0.517. It tests ether-position transfer from the differently arranged bromodimethoxybenzene and low-retention bromobenzodioxole observations; their loading conditions differ.

Cyclohexyl acrylate at 50/1 and 150 uL is predicted at 12.94/22.91 mL. Its strong-eluent observation and the measured constrained bicyclic acrylate provide structural references. This tests weak-eluent transfer across ester-side ring environments while retaining amount differences.

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing scaffolds require different solvent-response scales and transition locations. Amino-nitrile labels establish large 5/1 completion volumes and positional onset differences, while amino-esters and 2-phenylpyridine show different response scales. Intermediate transitions and transfer to other nitrogen environments remain incompletely identified.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Intermediate labels can prevent corrections learned for amino carbonyls from distorting amino nitriles, enamines or basic heteroaromatics.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do amino-nitrile positional differences develop, and do lutidine, methylquinoline and aminocrotonate follow their proposed intermediate response scales under the recorded loading conditions?

hypotheses.content: Nitrobenzophenone does not yet support one reliable solvent-response curve across recorded amounts. Completion decreases from 10/1 to 50/1 at 100 uL, whereas it increases sharply from 20/1 to 50/1 at 50 uL. A reproducible amount interaction and label variability remain competing explanations.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This region has produced large historical errors in opposite directions. A matched stronger-eluent series can constrain response shape without teaching a universal reversed solvent response.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the 100 uL measurements at 2/1 and 5/1 show ordinary growth toward the measured 10/1 endpoint, or do they reveal a broader nonmonotonic response? Replication would still be needed to establish repeatability.

hypotheses.content: Hydroxyl environment affects onset, completion and transition location separately. The latest naphthylethanol result rejects its proposed onset decrease, and bromobenzyl alcohol shows a much sharper 5/1-to-10/1 change than a generic donor-count adjustment would capture.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Labels spanning primary, remote secondary and benzylic secondary alcohols can constrain local structural interactions and reduce incorrect sharing of endpoint slopes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the matched remote-secondary-alcohol pair show modest or steep growth between 2/1 and 5/1, and is 1-phenylethanol's predicted 5/1 dip supported?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl and ether arrangement governs response transfer more strongly than acceptor count alone. The cyclopropyl beta-ketoester has a large measured weak-eluent response, while ethyl acetoacetate, dibenzyl ether and bromobenzodioxole show smaller responses under their supplied conditions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Carbonyls and ethers occupy much of the catalog. Local response labels and structural comparisons can teach interactions among functional-group placement, steric environment and solvent strength.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which parts of the large beta-ketoester response transfer to alpha substitution, bulky ester groups and multi-oxygen diesters, and which carbonyl or ether arrangements retain modest responses?

hypotheses.content: Benzyl benzoate develops a larger weak-eluent onset increase than isobutyl benzoate under their matched within-molecule loading conditions. The location of benzyl benzoate's increase between 30/1 and 100/1 remains unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The 100/1 label exposed an onset-specific failure. An intermediate condition can identify response shape without requiring onset and completion to share a slope.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 50/1, has benzyl benzoate onset already increased substantially, or is most growth concentrated between 50/1 and 100/1?

hypotheses.content: Cinnamic acid completion increases from 2/1 to 5/1 at the recorded 2000 uL DCM loading-solvent volume. Whether its broad interval and solvent response transfer unchanged to 1500 uL is unresolved; a loading-solvent-volume effect remains an untested hypothesis.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The paired conditions test a recorded loading feature in a region with broad measured intervals, without attributing behavior to absent concentration or solution variables.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the 1500 uL measurements preserve the 2000 uL response scale at both ratios, or does changing loading-solvent volume alter onset and completion differently?

hypotheses.content: The formally charged P/O structure has a large measured rise between 2/1 and 10/1, but its intermediate curvature is unmeasured. Sulfoxide feedback provides a response-shape comparison without establishing the same mechanism or curve for P/O.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A matched intermediate label can constrain response shape in a rare atom/charge environment and improve transfer beyond the oxygen and nitrogen environments dominating coverage.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 5/1, is the P/O response near the predicted intermediate value, or is most growth concentrated on one side of that ratio?

feedback_interpretation: Sulfoxide's latest 2/1 and 5/1 measurements connect coherently to its measured 10/1 endpoint, so its transition is now sufficiently anchored to redirect acquisition toward the P/O intermediate. Nitrobenzophenone's 50 uL completion rose sharply between 20/1 and 50/1, weakening transfer of the earlier declining response across amounts; the conflicting 100 uL endpoint remains unresolved. Bromonitrobenzene instead showed modest additional completion growth. Amino-nitrile completion was historically underestimated for both isomers, with a substantially later para onset, motivating intermediate labels. Naphthylethanol's latest result rejects its predicted onset dip, while bromobenzyl alcohol emphasizes transition-location errors. The cyclopropyl beta-ketoester failure strengthens topology-specific carbonyl interpretation. Benzyl benzoate's 100/1 onset increase contrasts with isobutyl benzoate's modest onset change. Cinnamic acid completion increased, contradicting its predicted decrease. Isobutyrophenone's midpoint supports a graded amount association with nearly stable completion, but all three amounts are now measured. These errors are historical acquisition errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch combines failure repair with focused transfer tests. Matched nitrobenzophenone conditions address conflicting observations; amino-nitrile intermediates, a remote-alcohol pair, cinnamic-acid loading-solvent comparisons, and intermediates for benzyl benzoate and P/O constrain response shape. Beta-ketoester comparisons vary carbonyl environment, alpha substitution and ester-side bulk. Additional aromatic carbonyls and ethers test whether those relationships generalize to common catalog chemistry, including modest predicted retention. The new biphenyl-ketone pair supplies a local response curve rather than an isolated novel endpoint. Loading differences remain explicit, and conflicting labels are not automatically treated as causal loading effects. Interchangeable amount variants and duplicate tuples are generally omitted because they offer little additional discrimination. Quantile widths are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and V2 minus V1 is treated as elution-interval behavior. All 32 IDs and their supplied predictions are fixed before any new label reveal.
